title: Tamil Nadu Monsoon Patterns and General Sowing Windows
source: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University — general agro-climatic guidance
topic: monsoon, sowing calendar, southwest monsoon, northeast monsoon
content:
Tamil Nadu's rainfall pattern is somewhat different from much of India: while the Southwest Monsoon (roughly June-September) brings the bulk of rainfall to most of the country, Tamil Nadu receives a significant share of its annual rainfall from the Northeast Monsoon (roughly October-December), particularly in the delta and southern districts. This shapes local cropping calendars.

Kuruvai paddy is generally sown with the onset of Southwest Monsoon rains/canal water release (June-July), suited to areas with earlier water availability. Samba paddy, the main long-duration season in delta districts, is typically sown August-September to make use of Northeast Monsoon rains through the growing period.

Rainfed crops such as groundnut and pulses in many parts of the state are commonly sown with the onset of reliable rains, which farmers should confirm against current-season India Meteorological Department (IMD) monsoon onset and forecast updates rather than a fixed calendar date, since monsoon onset timing varies year to year.

Because a wrong sowing window is one of the most common avoidable causes of crop stress and yield loss, farmers are generally advised to combine traditional local sowing calendars with current-season IMD forecasts and any state agriculture department advisories before finalizing sowing dates each year.
